content:
Many times per day I will do something simple such as renaming a file that causes a dozen other files in my codebase to turn red with the error

Imports are out of date and must be rebuilt; use the "Restart File" command in your editor.

So I then have to manually open each of those files and run the restart file command. It is a tedious process, and really the only negative experience I have with the tooling.

There should be some way to tell VSCode "Restart all files that say they their imports need to be rebuilt" as a singular command.

I tried Restart Server, but this does not work on it's own, the files still say they need to be rebuilt after restarting the server. It does work if I also run lake build inside the terminal, but lake build only works if there are not any errors anywhere in the entire codebase, forcing me to shift my attention to focusing on fixing those errors or commenting them out temporarily, which would take more time than manually calling Restart File on the files whose imports need to be rebuilt.
Restart file works for the current file regardless of if there are errors in another file, so it should be possible to bypass lake build and simply restart all files necessary.

Have you tried the 'Build Project' command, which stops the server, builds the project and restarts it?

Note that lake build builds everything that it can build, so if your file does not have any dependencies with errors (which would also prevent 'Restart File'), it will work after lake build even if there are other files in the project that still have errors.

That seems to work. It is a bit heavy though, 10-20 seconds of standing by waiting for "processing". I assume if we made a "Restart all out-of-date files", which would just run Restart File for all out-of-date files, that would be much faster? A couple seconds I assume, (can they be ran in parallel?).

In Lean 3 editing a file in VS Code and then switching to another file which imports the edited file would automatically trigger a rebuild. I liked this behaviour because it was always what I wanted. A couple of times I have been caught out by the change of behaviour in Lean 4 where I make an edit and then check to see how it affects the later file and it doesn't affect it at all, and I am completely confused until I remember to click the button. If there were an option to make "rebuild automatically" the default I would immediately switch it on in all my projects. But I asked about this years ago (when the change occurred) and my impression at that time was that it would be difficult to change this?

@Kevin Buzzard See vscode-lean4#693 for previous discussion. I hope to get back to this some time later this year.

That said, personally, I don't remember what we used to call "orange bar hell" too fondly :-)

I remember orange bar hell and I totally take your point! However I think orange bar hell is less misleading than "this file is compiling right now but actually doesn't reflect the current state of your project", which I personally think is counterintuitive despite the non-hell benefits ("it still works, it's just telling the wrong story"). This might simply reflect the way I work with Lean and might not be representative of the broader community's use cases? Not sure.

Kevin Buzzard said:

this file is compiling right now but actually doesn't reflect the current state of your project

Note that despite the fact that you can still use the language server on the file that is now stale and don't have to wait for the whole project to rebuild every time you touch a file before you can work again, Lean tells you that it is stale:

(this message shows up regardless of where in the file your cursor is)

As for the whole 'Restart File' workflow and as mentioned in vscode-lean4#693, I'm not happy with the current workflow, either. We will hopefully improve it in the future.
I am good at missing this message. I am usually looking at a gigantic goal state or a huge trace, and am oblivious to everything else. Maybe this is a me problem :-)

In lean.nvim (where of course I have an entirely different userbase with different skillsets) I added a hook for this just recently. So now users can essentially configure:

  • follow VSCode, never restart/rebuild automatically
  • restart always, by adding 2 lines to their config
  • some custom logic they come up with, e.g. "only restart in project XYZ which is small, but not mathlib where that might be very expensive"

(If you ask me for in-depth docs, I'll tell you I haven't added them yet :), so that's coming, but it's the on_imports_out_of_date callback from https://github.com/Julian/lean.nvim/wiki/The-lean.nvim-Manual#full-configuration--settings )

I have also had this of experience of modifying a file, switching to another file that uses it, and then spend a few minutes not understanding why there is still an error in this file, only to realize that I need to rebuild the import to get the new behavior.

My cobebase is light, I don't use Mathlib or Batteriers, so restarting a file only takes a couple seconds. I absolutely would turn on automatic file restarts if it were an option.

Have you tried enabling the setting lean4.automaticallyBuildDependencies?
I think it only affects files which go red, not files that are working but with an outdated dependency,
but perhaps if you then restart the server as well it would make all open files go red and then auto-restart.
#general > PR to automatically "Restart File" when dependencies change
